Closest to nervaluate 'ent_type' but greedy.

published_reference.citation: Zhang, Jensen, Sonniks, Plank (2022). SkillSpan: Hard and Soft Skill Extraction from English Job Postings. NAACL-HLT 2022, pp. 4962-4984. doi:10.18653/v1/2022.naacl-main.366
published_reference.table: Table 5 (Appendix E), TEST rows; columns SKILL / KNOWLEDGE / COMBINED x STL / MTL; span-F1 x100
comparability: The paper's TEST split has 4,680 sentences from BIG+HOUSE+TECH (Table 2); the HF release used here has only HOUSE+TECH (3,569 sentences; the paper lists 1,216+2,352=3,568), because BIG was not released.

The paper scores ALL test sentences, including those without skills; the repo's anchor 0.670 is on the 974-sentence subset with gold spans, which cannot contain false positives on skill-free sentences.
Label mapping: SkillSpan SKILL = repo SOFT_SKILL, KNOWLEDGE = repo HARD_SKILL; COMBINED (STL) = the two single-task models' spans merged, closest to the repo's labelled micro exact-span F1.
